newsitem.title: UK: Most bond markets climb, Japan only loser - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Most bond markets climb, Japan only loser - Salomon.

text.p: Most bond markets moved higher in the latest week with Japan being the only one to buck the upward trend, according to data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
Speculation earlier in the week over a possible interest rate rise in Japan helped to drive JGBs 0.63 percent lower in local currency terms, while Ireland was the star performer with gains of 1.04.

Irish bonds were boosted by soft U.S. inflation data and followed other markets higher while the Irish punt continued to look strong. In line with expectations, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Thursday called a national election to be held on June 6.
The Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index gained 0.37 percent in local currency terms for the week ended May 14.
Other top gainers were British gilts and government bonds in France, Sweden and Spain.
Gilts returned 0.96 percent in the week in local currency terms. French debt gave investors 0.84 percent, Swedish bonds gained 0.83 percent and Spanish bonos climbed 0.85 percent.
Italian BTPs and German Bunds made more humble gains of 0.69 percent and 0.44 percent respectively in local currency terms.
For dollar-based investors the picture was different as Japan posted the highest gains amid continuing weakness in dollar/yen, which has lost around ten percent of its value over the last few weeks.
JGBs were way out in front with a climb of 4.85 percent in dollar terms, followed by a dollar gain of 2.55 percent for Swedish bonds.
All bond markets posted gains in dollar terms, and U.S. Treasuries offered returns of 0.51 percent.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
